observations: Only 4 closed trades; estimates may be unstable.
assumptions: Synthetic unlevered long/short OHLCV research; provider perpetual prices do not model perpetual execution.
Free cash plus reserved entry notional plus unrealized P&L equals equity; short proceeds are unavailable.
Market signals only. No stops, targets, limit orders, pyramiding, borrowing, funding or liquidation.
Completed-bar signals execute after the captured delay at an eligible open; warm-up bars cannot trade.
Passive benchmark allocates all capital to buy-and-hold, applying identical entry costs and quantity rules; segment close costs apply when positions close at boundaries.
Spread is half per side, separate from slippage; prices round adversely to tick and quantities down to step.
Arbitrary trusted Python can access files/network and introduce look-ahead bias; this is not a security sandbox.

scriptInspection.policy: ast-v1; exponential seed residual <= 1e-6; conservative summed lookbacks

seeds.limitation: User-created generators and external nondeterminism must be seeded by strategy code.

assessment.label: Insufficient evidence
reasons: Final holdout and chronological validation have not both been completed.
assessment.text: Insufficient evidence. Historical profitability: the original run returned 0.33% after its modeled fees, spread and slippage. That captured evaluation result is descriptive and does not by itself establish repeatability. Out-of-sample evidence is unavailable. Repeatability and benchmark-relative evidence are screened separately using chronological validation, expanding walk-forward folds, a frozen final holdout, cost and execution-delay stress, parameter neighbors and concentration. Final holdout and chronological validation have not both been completed. Remaining uncertainty: these are conservative, versioned screening rules, not a calibrated probability of alpha or future profitability. The passive price benchmark does not establish risk-adjusted alpha. Synthetic OHLCV execution omits borrowing, margin, liquidation and order-book behavior. Funding and impact are included only when captured in the run configuration, with the limitations in its assumptions. Prefix checks sample only a few cutoffs and cannot certify arbitrary Python against look-ahead bias or external data access. Known local trials do not reveal all prior strategy selection. PBO and Deflated Sharpe are not reported because complete selection-history inputs are unavailable. Forward paper observation with the frozen strategy and realistic execution costs is required before drawing stronger conclusions.
